agent_loop.recall: No peeking — name the 4 steps of the agent loop, in order.
agent_loop.answer: perceive → decide → act → observe, then loop

agent_vs_chatbot.recall: In one line: what makes an agent different from a chatbot?
agent_vs_chatbot.answer: an agent ACTS via tools, observes the result, and loops; a chatbot just replies

llm_core.recall: What is the LLM's job inside an agent?
llm_core.answer: it's the reasoning core — it decides the next action; your code executes it

tool_is_fn.recall: When a model 'uses a tool', whose code actually runs the function?
tool_is_fn.answer: YOUR code runs it; the model only requests the call

tool_schema.recall: What part of a tool makes the model decide WHEN to use it?

tool_boundary.recall: Where do agents fail most, and how do you design for it?
tool_boundary.answer: at the tool boundary — wrap calls, return a clean error string the model can read, retry

context_limit.recall: Why does an agent 'forget' earlier steps — what's the limit called?
context_limit.answer: the finite context window; old turns fall out

memory_types.recall: Short-term vs long-term memory in an agent — what goes in each?
memory_types.answer: short = this task's turns; long = facts/preferences persisted across tasks

rag.recall: What does RAG do for an agent?
rag.answer: retrieves only the relevant chunks (vector search) and feeds them into context

decomposition.recall: What does planning let an agent do that a single call can't?
decomposition.answer: break a big goal into sub-steps, execute them, and re-plan

react.recall: What is the ReAct / plan-execute loop?
react.answer: reason → act → observe the result → reason again

self_correction.recall: How does a good agent self-correct mid-task?
self_correction.answer: it observes the failed result and re-plans instead of charging ahead

stopping.recall: Two ways to stop an agent loop safely?

handoffs.recall: Why split work across multiple agents?
handoffs.answer: specialised roles do their part better; an orchestrator routes between them

orchestrator.recall: What does an orchestrator do in a multi-agent system?
orchestrator.answer: routes work to the right worker agent and manages handoffs

evaluation.recall: How do you actually KNOW an agent works (not just in the demo)?
evaluation.answer: an eval harness — test cases scored automatically, not vibes

guardrails.recall: Name two production guardrails an agent needs.
guardrails.answer: input validation, output checks, retries, cost caps

cost.recall: What drives an agent's cost, and one way to cut it?
cost.answer: tokens × turns; trim context / cache / fewer loops / cheaper model
